title: Knowledge check: End-to-End Algorithm Design

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly part of “End-to-End Algorithm Design”?
options: Translating Requirements Into a Problem Model
An unrelated topic outside this lesson
questions.answer_key: Translating Requirements Into a Problem Model
questions.explanation: The attached PDF lists “Translating Requirements Into a Problem Model” under lesson 147, “End-to-End Algorithm Design”. The complete syllabus list is retained in this lesson file.

questions.prompt: When applying “End-to-End Algorithm Design”, which approach supports a reliable solution?
options: State assumptions and invariants, test normal and edge cases, and analyze time/space costs.
Rely only on one successful example.
Ignore input constraints and empty inputs.
Choose the most complex data structure by default.
questions.answer_key: State assumptions and invariants, test normal and edge cases, and analyze time/space costs.
questions.explanation: Algorithm design requires explicit assumptions, a reasoned method, and tests; lesson 147 remains draft until its technical detail is reviewed.

questions.prompt: After sketching a solution for “End-to-End Algorithm Design”, what should you record?
options: A known input, trace, expected result, edge case, and complexity rationale.
Only the final code with no tests.
A timing result from one very small input as a proof of complexity.
questions.answer_key: A known input, trace, expected result, edge case, and complexity rationale.
questions.explanation: A reproducible worked example and boundary tests make assumptions visible; theoretical complexity should be justified from the algorithm, not inferred from one timing.
